messages.subject: Elite configurations are all the same
parts:
I ran irace as a quick test to see what kind of results I get with a very low runtime for my algorithms (it really takes a LOT of time).

I found that I get essentially the same configuration as elite configurations 5 times.
I thought that irace performs statistical tests and discards configurations that are not significantly different.

606  --alg ILS --pertstr 0.03 --maxrt 3
625  --alg ILS --pertstr 0.03 --maxrt 3

Sincerely,
Andreas

messages.subject: Re: Elite configurations are all the same
parts:
(Reposting here without the data in case it is useful for someone else)

Hi Andreas,

The seed should not affect too much the results. It is just a variance reduction technique.

I plotted the frequency that the parameters are sampled using parameterFrequency() and the algorithms seem to be sampled almost equally with a small advantage for ILS, However, looking at the parameter space, it seems that once the ILS is chosen, the other parameters are mostly disabled, so there is not much diversity there.

Looking at the avg rank per algorithm type, it seems ILS is often the best (probably conditional to the parameters found by irace). See boxplot.

Looking at the restarts, they are happening every iteration, so irace is already trying to increase diversity by sampling. At least for now, irace does not have any niching mechanism to enforce diversity, it only increases diversity by sampling more widely, but if the new solutions are worse, they will get eliminated and lose diversity again.

The R code I used for my analysis is attached.

This is an interesting benchmark because the parameter space is very unbalanced. It would be even more interesting if you can find a better non-ILS configuration without prior knowledge in the same amount of experiments (consistently in independent runs since irace could also find that configuration by chance). It would clearly show something that should be improved in irace.

If you want to do a test, I would suggest to do additional runs of irace. Adding more budget (longer runs of irace) is not going to help because it seems too easy to get trapped in good ILS configurations.

Thanks,

Manuel.
